assignment.context: Glaucon presents an account of justice for Socrates to examine. Distinguish that account from your own position. You do not need knowledge of the rest of the book.
assignment.question: Would justice still matter morally if it brought no practical advantages, such as safety or a good reputation? Explain your position and relate it to the account in the passage.

passages.text: They say that to do injustice is, by nature, good; to suffer injustice, evil; but that the evil is greater than the good.

And so when men have both done and suffered injustice and have had experience of both, not being able to avoid the one and obtain the other, they think that they had better agree among themselves to have neither; hence there arise laws and mutual covenants; and that which is ordained by law is termed by them lawful and just.

turns.text: In the passage, they make the agreement so they can do more injustice to other people.
